Oneg Shabbat — Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's portion (Emor)

[Oneg Shabbat — the weekly portion; followed by an exegetical article by Hirsh Niebelski of Kielce.] Torah sayings, remarks and anecdotes on this week's Torah portion.
Collected and styled by Yehuda.
Parashat Emor
The Portion
—o—
a) "And ye shall keep My commandments... and ye shall not profane My holy name" (Lev. 22:31 [printed "כר. לא."])
It turns out that even by performing commandments ("And ye shall keep My commandments") one can also desecrate God's name ("and ye shall not profane My holy name") — when one does not mean the commandments seriously, but exploits them for certain purposes... Beit Yaakov.
—o—
b) "These are My appointed seasons" (23:2)
The prophet Isaiah says: "Your new moons and your appointed feasts My soul hateth." When the holidays become "your feasts" — only your own holidays, and not God's and not the poor man's — then "My soul hateth". [Then] God hates them, because "these are My appointed seasons": the festivals must be God's alone and not merely yours; one must also take care of the poor man, so that he too may know of Sabbath and holiday... Orach Chaim.
—o—
c) "Neither shall they shave off the corner of their beard" (21:5)
Rabbi Eizel Charif travelled around the country with a work of his own. Once he comes to a small town and meets a maskil, a clean-shaven man, who needles him:
— Why do our rabbis keep on writing books? Are our old books too few, then?
Reb Eizel answers him:
— A Jew usually keeps the hairs of his beard in a book, and that is why so many new books are needed nowadays — because of the growing number of the clean-shaven...
* * *
The Kelmer Maggid [of Kelmė] once rebuked a group of maskilim for[?] shaving their beards. He asked them: What will you plead in the world to come?
One of the maskilim answers:
— We will answer: just as we came into the world without a beard, so we also come there without a beard...
— If so — answers the Maggid — pull out your teeth too, for you came into the world without teeth, after all...
—o—
d) "And ye shall eat neither bread, nor parched corn, nor fresh ears, until this selfsame day."
We count the Omer from the day on which it became permitted to eat the new grain until the day of the Giving of the Torah.
For counting connects things, links them together, and grain and Torah belong together — "If there is no flour, there is no Torah". The Maharal of Prague.
—o—
e) "And ye shall take you on the first day."
"The first for the reckoning of sins." Tractate Sukkah.
Sukkot is called "the season of our rejoicing" — and if one begins on it to count the sins, what then is the joy in it? But the reckoning of sins is for a different purpose. Since around the Days of Awe Jews repent, and if one repents, then wilful sins turn into merits, transgressions turn into commandments; therefore one counts the sins of the Jews in order to credit them as commandments... and that is the joy. Or Yesharim.
* * *
In a similar way the Baal Shem [Tov] interprets the verse: "In that day the iniquity of the house of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none" (Jeremiah 50). Why will the sins of the Jews be sought "in that day"?
— In order to credit them as commandments... Maor va-Shemesh.
The Haftarah
—o—
f) "And they shall come near to My table, to minister unto Me, and they shall keep My charge" (Ezekiel 44)
"And they shall come near to My table" — why is it specifically the table that is mentioned?
Because the table symbolises — according to the Midrash — wealth, and that is why the table stood on the north side, for "out of the north cometh gold" [printed "צפון זהב יאתה"].
The prophet says that even those who will come to the table, to wealth, will also keep "My charge" — and this is indeed a prophecy for the future... Ahavat Yehonatan.
Avot
—o—
g) "And he who commits one transgression acquires for himself one accuser" (4:13)
From every transgression — the Rebbe Reb Zusha used to say — an accuser is created, an evil angel; but I have seen these very angels that were created from the transgressions of Jews, and I saw that they are all cripples: one is without a hand, the other without a foot. For do Jews commit transgressions with their whole heart? And just as their transgressions are groaning and broken, so are the angels that are created by the transgressions... Butzina Kadisha.
—o—
Important Explanations of Today's Portion.
"Emor", chapter 21, on verse 1: "There shall none be defiled for the dead" — the Rashbam says, among other things: "For his brother and for his sister he shall not defile himself (in many Chumashim it reads "yitama") for them, and it is not said 'for them'" (in many Chumashim it reads "bahem"). The quoted passage in the Rashbam is quite incomprehensible, and it is a wonder that nobody has paid attention to it until today. In my opinion printing errors have surely crept in here, and it should read thus: "And for his brother and for his sister etc. for her he may defile himself, for them, although it is not said 'for them'". That is to say, the Rashbam joins the end of verse 2, "and for his brother", with verse 3, which he quotes in full up to "for her he may defile himself", and here he adds his own word: "for them" — stressing thereby that "for her he may defile himself" must be understood as "for them he may defile himself", although "for them" is not written, because he may defile himself not only for a sister but for all the relatives listed together.
"Emor", chapter 23, on verse 40: "And ye shall take you on the first day" — Ibn Ezra says: "And the exile from the land of Kedar to the land of Edom, if he has eyes, will know the secret of this commandment". Countless explanations have already been offered on this passage, none of which is satisfactory. In my opinion, however, Ibn Ezra is speaking here about himself; that is, he, who was driven from the land of Kedar — that is Spain — to the land of Edom — that is Italy — knows the secret of the commandment. And the words "if he has eyes" were added in later times by someone who did not understand Ibn Ezra's style and correct meaning, and afterwards it all got mixed together in the printing houses. As is known, Ibn Ezra was born and brought up in southern Spain, which in his books he always calls by the name "land of Kedar"; from there, for [certain] reasons, he fled to Italy, which he calls the land of Edom, and there he composed his commentary on the Torah.
In a similar way I also explain the passage in Ibn Ezra on the portion Acharei Mot, 16, on verse 8, where he says: "And when you are thirty-three years old you will know it". Various explanations were given on this passage many hundreds of years ago (see the commentary of Nachmanides, the responsa of the Maharam of Rothenburg, Daat Zekenim of the Tosafists, etc.). In my opinion, however, Ibn Ezra was 33 years old when he wrote these words, and he says to the young pupil or reader: when you are 33 years old like me, you too will know the secret of the scapegoat for Azazel. One quite often hears such a manner of speaking from older people to younger ones.
I hope that everyone who thinks logically and is versed in the style of our old commentators will acknowledge my explanations as the simplest and the most correct.
Hirsh Niebelski [?], Kielce.

It is already turning green.

Where Does the Dacha Come From? — Scientific Discoveries

[Der Kokh-lefl — humour.] Scientific discoveries.

A group of married men came before the Lord of the Universe with a request. — Why, they argued, are we, Your children, worse off than all Your other creatures?
Lord of the Universe! Why have You punished us with wives, from whom we suffer more than all the other creatures, and we never have any rest from them?

Taken from a [sacred] book and retold by "Kokh-lefl".
A Little Letter to the Dollar

[Der Kokh-lefl — humour, economic crisis.] — You surely want to know, Mister Dollar, what is new with your friend [pshiatshel, Polish przyjaciel] — the złoty. Unfortunately I cannot pass on any regards from him to you — because I have not seen him for who knows[?] how long... and in general one sees him very little in the street... They say, Mister Dollar, that you have fallen under the pressure of the English pound... That is, you are sick with the English disease [rickets; a pun]. It seems to me, Mister Dollar, that falling is somehow no business, for in the end you will have to "fall in" [come to grief]...
All the young ladies [panienki], Mister Dollar, envy you your success [powodzenie], although the young men know your real age and see your greened face... and still they fall in love with you at first sight.. They, the young men, do not look at the bride at all, they only look at the dollar... That's what I call success!
Only one thing about you surprises me! You have been in America so long already, and yet you are still a "greenhorn"...
Yours, Yehuda Friedman.

[History — antisemitism in 19th-century Germany; serialized article, concluding part.]
Philosophers, poets and historians take part in the agitation. — The financial crash in Germany in 1873 and the revenge on Jews for it. — The blood libel in Konitz [today Chojnice] in 1900. — Germany gives Jews rights and takes them back. — The changed situation after the year [18]70. — Further descriptions of Jewish-German relations.
By Sh. Rozenfeld.

End.
But the nearer the revolutionary year, the more boldly Jewish self-defence comes forward. And in the general German Landtag of 1847 the Prussian ministers are booed when they declare that "Jewish equal rights do not accord with the spirit of a Christian state." Even Bismarck speaks out for Jewish equal rights with only one condition: that they should not occupy such positions where "the Christian citizen would have to obey the Jewish official"...

3.
The revolution of 1848 brings Jews equal rights — but not for long. The heavily "fixed" [in quotation marks] Prussian constitution of 1850 even guarantees the Jews equal rights, but hardly has the constitution been published when a terrible agitation starts again against what had "destroyed the whole foundation of a Christian state" — and the agitation was led by a baptized Jew, Stahl [Friedrich Julius Stahl]. Other writers and scholars joined him. The air was full of theories and splinters of theories, with modern words and badly understood expressions, and everything argued that Jewish equal rights are the greatest misfortune for every Christian state. The wildest plans for how to get rid of the Jews are heard everywhere. The ministers listen to it and by circulars they order throughout the Prussian province that Jews be removed from the schools as teachers and from the courts — as judges and defence lawyers.
In the parliament of 1861 the majority expressed its protest against the ministers who had issued circulars contrary to the constitution, but the same parliament also showed how great a number of antisemites sit in parliament and express the will and the opinions of the German people. Against that one protest there were heard many, many fiery antisemitic speeches, wholly in the spirit of Stahl and his comrades.
But not only within the walls of parliament was the antisemitic talk heard, but also in the street, through literature. Books are written and daily newspapers appear, such as the "Kreuzzeitung", in which the Jew is the main subject. Besides the professors, the musicians of genius, Richard Wagner and Franz Liszt, also exerted themselves against the Jews. The former reproached the Jews that what they create in music smells of Semitism, of race; therefore their music is a misfortune for the kosher Teuton. And Liszt argued that the Jewish composer cannot express his national "I". And what Mendelssohn or Halévy wrote, a Christian composer could also have written. And because it is "nothing new", there is no need to give them equal rights [printed with a misprint]...
But despite the great all-German anti-Jewish intrigue, united Germany came and, through the Bundesrat and the Reichstag and the signature of the King — on the third of July 1869 — abolished all Jewish restrictions, and the German Jews became citizens with equal rights.
Barely a few years had passed, however, and again an antisemitic agitation against Jews began. The victory of the Germans in the Franco-German war (1870–1871) brings into Germany 5 milliard in money. The banks are full of free capital, the population begins to create various enterprises, to found various joint-stock companies. A great boom sets in; various securities and shares climb sky-high [lit. "into the world"]. People become rich overnight — a good time; but hardly had two years passed in the great tumult around the money-dust when there came a tremendous crash, as is known to us.
And who is guilty of the general crash? The Jews. And together with the Jews the government is guilty, which gave the Jews the right to trade and to swindle according to their evil will. The Jews, and with them the German liberals, are guilty of Germany's misfortune. New newspapers are created, new organizations arise and new people appear, and all together pour out their wrath and their patriotic hysteria upon the Jews. The people listen. Historians, clergymen and philosophers such as Treitschke, Stoecker and Dühring fire off the "big word", hold the most fiery speeches and write heavy books, and all this is meant to prove the worthlessness of the Jews and their depravity, and the importance [?; printed "vikhsikeyt"] of the Germans and their loftiness. And if other historians and other scholars come, like Mommsen and Virchow, and say a good word for the Jews, they are laughed at and decried. New antisemitic parties arise. They unite, crumble and gather again. Antisemitic literature grows and works and penetrates the whole people. The antisemitic party disappears only when every other party, except the Social Democratic one, is itself already permeated with the antisemitic spirit. And from now on German antisemitic literature, with its "principles" and "conditions", counts as a model for the theoretical and practical antisemitism of the whole world.
Thus the Jews enter the 20th century with curtailed rights, with injured honour, with a thick atmosphere of hatred around them and with the shadow of a blood libel (in Konitz 1900) behind them.
At the same time the German Jews fought with o n e hand for their rights and their honour; with the o t h e r hand they created a great literature of Jewish, chiefly historical, scholarship and a strong communal organization. And with b o t h hands they create and found the well-known assimilationist theory of "Germans of the Mosaic faith", which denies the national element of the Jewish people, because, they say, Jews are not a people but a religious sect within Germandom.
And the great majority of German Jewry is to this very day faithful to these theories with all their further implications.
———
And now people wonder: how can it be that the majority of the German people should hand itself over into the hands of such a scoundrel as Hitler is, and accept as good his man-eating, antisemitic methods of government? The answer is right at hand:
— An inheritance, friend reader, a sad inheritance has Germany received from her distant and recent past. An inheritance of philosophers, poets, historians, musicians and plain antisemites. A whole world could be poisoned with the fruits of the antisemitic culture that accumulated in Germany, even in the 19th century alone. In what Hitler preaches and demands now there is not a single original idea. "Everything has already been" and "there is nothing new" in the Hitlerite paradise. Even the boycott, even the "castration" that he demanded, he finds ready in the pogrom programmes of his predecessors. Even an elephant, if one stuffed it with the whole patriotic literature, would also go mad — so why should such a beast as Hitler is not go mad from it? And so indeed he did.. And there are no more wonders in the world and no more miracles. Everything has its cause. And everything has its historical-social explanation.
In the Children's World.

[Children's corner — special Lag BaOmer supplement; nature story.] A special section of the "Zaglembier Tsaytung" in honour of Lag BaOmer, for our little ones. Compiled by Sh. Libas Zohn [?].

Spring in the Village.
By Mendele Moykher Sforim.

A beautiful, warm spring day. The golden sun, on rising, tore apart and scattered the big clouds in the air, and with her shining face looked down from the blue sky, gently, kindly, upon the earth. God's creatures, all of them, from great to small, shaking themselves out of the long winter sleep, have lively and merrily each set about their own business; fresh yellow flowers poke their little heads out from among the young green grass, peep out and look charming. The willows by the river hurry to put on their new green cloaks, mirroring themselves in the water — pure, clear and silver.
From the far-off warm lands, there in foreign parts, the birds come back here in flocks [?] to their rest; wild geese splash somewhere among the rushes here in the river, wild ducks whirl about the reeds, out and in, with a clamour, a twittering. Little swallows flutter, hover to and fro in the air; deeply absorbed in building, they repair new and old nests.
Welcome! The old familiar pair of storks is here too, luckily, in a good hour. She, the stork-wife, stands on one leg, her little head to one side, [still?], gazing at her old nest up on the top of a tree; and he, on his long stilts, strolls hoppingly [?] over the marsh there, looking on at a puddle where frogs jump and croak, and suddenly — peck-peck! — a snap, and into the red "Jewish" beak it goes...
There is life, joy, fluttering, buzzing, singing and twittering everywhere.
It is a holiday, it is springtime...
Daddy Is Sleeping. (A Story).

[Children's corner — story.] Etl's father is a dealer. He deals in old clothes. In the morning, when everyone is still asleep, he gets out of bed, dresses, takes his tallit and tefillin and goes to the beit midrash to pray.
When Daddy has eaten his breakfast, he takes the sack under his arm and sets off from courtyard to courtyard, calling out loud: "Handel! Handel!" [the old-clothes man's cry].
When Daddy already has a full sack of clothes, he goes off to a dealer in old goods and sells him the whole merchandise he has bought up during the day.
Towards evening Etele's father comes home very tired. He lies down to rest a little and slowly falls asleep.
Etele talks quietly and walks on tiptoe, so that Daddy will not wake from his sleep.
Etele loves her Daddy very much; every day she prays to God that Daddy should be healthy and strong and be able to support the family.

From the Jewish Legends

[Children's corner — rabbinic legends.] Collected by R.

1.
Once the government issued a decree that whoever put tefillin on his head would have his brain pierced. Now one man, Elisha, put on tefillin and went out into the market. He saw a government official, he ran away, and the other ran after him. When the other caught him, Elisha quickly took the tefillin off his head and held them in his hands. The official asks him: What have you got in your hands? Elisha answers him: — Dove's wings!
Elisha opened his hands, and indeed dove's wings were found there.
From then on he was called: "Elisha, the man of the wings."

2.
Rabbah bar bar Hana was once travelling with a caravan of Arabs; he ate, and forgot to say grace on the spot.
When the caravan had already gone some way, Rabbah bar bar Hana remembered that he had not said grace. He thinks to himself: What is to be done? If I tell the Arabs that I forgot to say grace and therefore want to go back to say it at the place where I ate, as Jewish law requires, they won't want to wait for me. They will say: Say grace here — it will reach God from anywhere. Better I shall say: Wait for me, because I forgot a golden dove at that place.
Rabbah bar bar Hana went back and said grace at the place where he had eaten, and found a golden dove there.
Good Qualities Befit Learning (from the Midrash)

[Children's corner — a parable from the Midrash.] A rich man once boasted to his friend that his wealth was very great:
— I have a thousand sacks of grain, a thousand jars of olive oil and a thousand barrels of wine.
His friend remarked to him:
— Do you have storehouses for all of this, to put each thing away in a safe place so that it will be preserved?
If you have room for all your wealth — he went on to tell the rich man — it belongs to you entirely. But if not, you own nothing, and the wind will carry off all your riches.
So it is when a person has learned much and is laden with much knowledge and Torah; one says to him:
— Do you also have good manners besides? Then the whole Torah belongs to you; but if not, you own nothing and your knowledge is going to be lost.
Every learned man who has good qualities in him is like a tree that is firmly rooted in the earth. And even if the strongest storm-winds come, they will not be able to move it from its place. Its leaves will always be green and it will not cease to bear fruit.

Będzin
The agitation for the meeting was conducted under the slogan "Judaism is in danger".
On Sunday the annual meeting of the members of the Gemilut Hesed (G"H, interest-free loan) fund of our town took place in the hall of the "Merchants' Association" (Sokhrim-Fareyn). Interest in the meeting was the same as in the election campaign for the first kehilla elections. Already several days before, the "little Jewish world" had been boiling like a cauldron. Factions of every kind racked their brains over composing the lists of candidates. Every day brought new conceptions and new "cabinet crises". Besides that, a recruiting drive was conducted among the members. Every side mobilised its forces, if only to prevent a victory of the "enemy" who wants to "grab the bank"...
On the Sabbath agitation was carried on in the Hasidic "shtiblekh" that everyone who wants "the sinners not to grab the bank, so that a Sabbath-observer can get a loan — should come to the meeting and save Judaism".
It goes without saying that the agitation had the proper success, and such a number of members came as no society has yet been privileged to see... Both halls of the "Merchants' Association" were packed full, and very many more remained outside, unable to get in any more.
The mood in the hall — a tense one; the "air" smells of gunpowder, the smallest "spark" can cause an explosion, but "the devil is not as terrible as he is painted". The meeting was nevertheless carried through to the end, with small incidents.
———
The meeting is opened by the chairman, Mr. L. Rubinlicht. The chair is handed over to Mr. M. Gold, who invites to the presidium Messrs. A. Lidubarski [Lidzbarski?], L. Strobel, and as secretary — Mr. Żmucki[?].
After the reading of the minutes of the last general meeting, a series of formal proposals of the board concerning changes to the statute are considered. Among the changes is also the paragraph on the term of office of the board. According to a circular (okólnik) of the "Joint" the board is elected for 3 years. Those assembled, seeing[?] a "danger" in the change, rejected this change too...
Around the proposals a discussion develops that leads to absurdities. The "speakers" do not grasp the actual question, they voice such opinions as cause tempers to become even more heated, and during the "votes" shouting is heard as at a mass rally..
Then come the reports: the treasury report — Mr. Montag; the audit committee — Mr. Herciger; and on the activity — the chairman Mr. Rubinlicht, who speaks of the importance of the fund at the present moment, when a decline prevails in the financial institutions. In the course of 14 months — says Mr. Rubinlicht — the outgoing board issued 738 loans for a sum of 144 thousand zł. Such a sum was also collected back, together with another 29 thousand zł. of old outstanding debts.
The outgoing board does not stop short of the most far-reaching measures against debtors. 103 borrowers are in court and 59 already with the komornik [bailiff]. Mr. Rubinlicht censures the former management, which caused losses of a good many thousands of zł. out of the collected people's pennies...
On the motion of the writer of these lines a protest resolution against the persecution of the Jews in Germany was adopted.
After the reports the "real" discussion only begins, in which "whatever anyone had on his heart, he spoke out". Among the criticism was also the "injustice" that in the presidium "religious Jewry is not represented", that the members of the presidium go bareheaded... and that Mr. Montag with his partners from the "Światowid" cinema do not want to pay the "pauszeczka" [lump-sum fee]...
Mr. Feigenblat censures the activity of the board so far; he expresses himself negatively about the reports given and proposes that a committee be elected to carry out a precise audit of the books and only then publish an exact report in the press. Mr. Feigenblat criticises the board for increasing the administrative expenses at a time when reductions are being made everywhere.
Mr. Rosenberg speaks out against the fact that a member from the popular masses can be granted a loan only after 8 months.
Also speaking are Messrs. Aharon Berenblat, Tenenbaum, Herzberg, Baruch, Herszlewicz, Kartusz and others, and after the reply of Mr. Rubinlicht and Mr. Liwer[?] the old board is granted an absolutorium (discharge).
The budget ("budoshet") for a sum of 18,320 zł. is passed on to the new board.
— Elections! Elections! The word simply electrified those assembled. In the name of "strengthening the faith" (khizek ha-das) Jews sacrificed themselves and with awe and love (bi-dekhilu u-rekhimu) campaigned for the "kosher candidates"...
About 220 men took part in the elections, and the results are as follows:
L. Bauszykowski[?], L. Rubinlicht, J. Goldfeler, A. D. Balimowski, M. M. Janowski, J. Wygodzki[?], M. Rozencaft[?], A. L. Grünwald, M. Hampel, Z. Lemberg, J. M. Kurland, A. M. Szwarcbaum, J. Rozinker[?], Ch. Braner, A. Frachcwajg.
As we are informed, a larger number of members have submitted a protest: 1) to the chairman of the general meeting, 2) to the outgoing chairman Mr. Rubinlicht and 3) to the Joint. The protest points out that 1) persons without the right to vote took part in the elections, and 2) people have entered the new board — undesirable elements who may undermine the authority of the institution.
A forest guard beats young Jews from Będzin murderously.

Two young men from Będzin went for a walk in the Grodziec forest; there they were met by the forest guard, who demanded of them a fine of 25 zł. each for walking along the forest road. When the young men declared that they had no money on them, the guard led them off to the office of the forest wardens, where the young men were cruelly beaten by the guard; there are deep wounds on their bodies.
The beaten young men went to the police duty office [?], where a report was drawn up about it, and the hooligan guard is being handed over to criminal justice.
Proceeds of the ball at Fürstenberg's gymnasium in Będzin

On 11 March of this year a ball was held at the Sz. Fürstenberg gymnasium in aid of the school's feeding campaign.
The net proceeds were 1,828 [?] zł. 98 gr. Of this sum, 738 zł. 55 gr. came in through the chairman of the gymnasium's supervisory board, Mr. Szymon Fürstenberg.
On this occasion the parents' committee expresses its thanks to the Fürstenberg family for their energetic work for the success of the ball.

Committee to combat the persecution of Jews in Germany.
As is known, a committee has been founded with the task of combating the persecution of Jews in Germany. At the head of the committee stands Dr. Weinzieher. The committee is located in the premises of the "Merchants' Association" and is active from 6.30 to 7.30 in the evening.

Pledge campaign of "Beit Lechem".
This Sabbath the society "Beit Lechem" has proclaimed a pledge (nedarim) campaign. Let every man called up to the Torah remember that "Beit Lechem" is the institution that gives bread to the hungry, and before every holiday a broad relief campaign is conducted.

A house-warming at the Będzin "Hitachdut".

On Saturday night a double celebration took place in the premises of "Hitachdut": the house-warming of the new premises and the farewell to the group "Hachana", which is leaving for hachshara. The hall, decorated with pictures of Gordon and Herzl, makes an imposing impression. The party orchestra plays "Hatikvah" and Dr. Rechtman opens the celebration, in the course of which he gives an overview of the work done. Greetings were given on behalf of the Zionist Organization by Mr. Wigodzki, of "Gordonia" by Herszlikowicz, Kibbutz Borochov by Anzelewicz, Hashachar, Keren Kayemet, Keren Hayesod, Hakoach and others. Then Mr. Josef Lewi of Łódź lectured on the subject "The situation in the movement". Later Mr. A. R. [?] Liwer bade farewell to those leaving for hachshara. On behalf of the group "Hachana" the youthful elder [?] replied with a fine speech.
The "living newspaper", written and read by Mr. Dawid Liwer, was received with great applause.
The farewells and dancing lasted until the grey of dawn.

On Saturday an extraordinary meeting will take place with the participation of Mr. Klarman, who will lecture on the subject "Why are we going to the 18th Congress?". After the lecture — discussion.
— On the same day a members' meeting of "Hachayil" will take place with the participation of a member of the Chief Command from Warsaw, who will lecture on the subject "The aims and tasks of 'Hachayil'".

Sosnowiec
"That's for the wrong you did my mother".
Epilogue of a family drama before the local district court.

In its time the family drama that happened in the Brandes family made a great impression among the Jewish population.
On 14 September 1932, at 3 in the afternoon, several revolver shots were heard from a house on Pusta Street in Pogoń. Soon afterwards a young man ran out of the house holding a revolver in his hand.
The young man ran to the police station, where, on coming in, he cried out:
— I've killed!
Later it turned out that the victim of the family tragedy was the 33-year-old Tauba Schwarz, who rented an apartment in that house on the second floor, and whose lover was Mr. Sz. Brandes of Sosnowiec.
Eight years ago Miss Schwarz had been taken on as a servant by the Brandes family. In the course of time close relations developed between her and Mr. Brandes, until it went so far that Brandes abandoned his wife and children and settled with his beloved in Częstochowa.
Because of his poor financial affairs he later came back with the "sweetheart" ("kochanka") to Sosnowiec, where he rented an apartment on Pusta Street, where the tragedy took place.
On that critical day the elder son of Brandes came into the apartment of his father's beloved and, crying out: "That's for the wrong done to my mother", fired 3 times and wounded her seriously.
The epilogue of the family drama took place before the local district court. After hearing the witnesses the court pronounced the verdict, according to which Brandes is sentenced to 4 years' prison.
Representative of Keren Kayemet protests against public Sabbath desecration by the motorcyclists.

As is known, a group of the Warsaw "Maccabi" is travelling on motorcycles to the Land of Israel. Last Saturday afternoon the group rode into Sosnowiec and stopped on Modrzejowska Street.
The public desecration of the Sabbath had an echo at the academy (festive evening) which the local "Maccabi" arranged in honour of the guests. The representative of the KKL, Mr. Mosze Jakub Karpin, greeted the guests and at the same time expressed a sharp protest in the name of the KKL committee.
"Mizrachi" announced in a letter that because of the Sabbath desecration it is not taking part.
The agreement between the Kehilla board and the Chevra Kadisha.

[Community — Chevra Kadisha and cemetery.]
At the Sunday meeting of the Kehilla board, together with the committee of the Chevra Kadisha (burial society), it was decided that the Chevra Kadisha will receive 25 percent of the income from burial plots and tombstones. In return, all the expenses of the cemetery will be covered by the Chevra Kadisha.
On the boycott action against German goods

[Boycott of Germany — Merchants' Association.]
In the premises of the "Merchants' Association" (Sokhrim-Fareyn) a meeting was held for the purpose of working out an exact programme for the boycott action against German goods.
After a lengthy discussion it was decided that the committee shall be formed only after the report has been heard of Mr. Józef Safer [?], who took part in the conference of the economic organisations.
Matches broken off because of... the fall of the dollar.

[Matchmaking and weddings — the dollar crisis.]
This coming Sunday falls Lag BaOmer, and many weddings had been fixed for that day. But now, because of the fall of the dollar, many bridegrooms have sent back the tna'im [engagement contracts] and refuse to go through with the wedding.
Recently, din-torahs [rabbinical lawsuits] were held at the Rabbinate over this matter. The bridegrooms demand that they be given dollars in... gold, and that the difference be added to the dowry money that was deposited in the banks.
From the World of Sport

[Będzin, Sosnowiec — sport.] “Hakoah” — “Victoria” (Częstochowa) 1:3.
On the “Hakoah” ground the friendly match between the two above-mentioned clubs took place; after an interesting fight it ended with a victory for “Hakoah” with a score of 1:3.
The guests, who now hold first place in the championship games of the Częstochowa district, displayed fine play in this match, but only while the score was 0:0. Only once they had conceded the first goal, and at the same time an accident befell their goalkeeper, did the guests become psychologically downcast, and the match was already lost for them.
With “Hakoah” the right side of the forward line played very weakly, especially Kalman, whose play brings disharmony into the attack. All the other players distinguished themselves very well. The goals were scored by Gutman 2 and Matil Rauen[?] 1. Referee Mazur — good.
• * •
On Sunday in Sosnowiec, in connection with the “P.Z.P.N. Day” [Polish Football Association], an interesting match took place between the representative team of “Upper Silesia” and the representative team of “Zagłębie”, which ended in a big victory for the Upper Silesians with a score of 6:0. A large part of the blame lies with the captain of the “Pod-Okręg”[?] [sub-district], who put the team together badly and showed that he has not yet grown up to such an important office. Throughout the match the Upper Silesians had a great “superiority”, so that the goalkeepers (up to the first half Nusberg[?], and in the second half Hirsz) are not at all to blame for the goals let in. Referee Mazur — good.
On Sunday an important championship match of Class “A” will take place in Sosnowiec between Będzin “Hakoah” and the “Police Club”. It is to be hoped that the “Hakoah” men will make every effort to win the two points, which are of colossal importance for them.
A. Wrocławski.
Legal Answers

[Law — answers to readers.] Mrs. R. A. — You can go to court and demand the release of your belongings from the execution (distraint) on the basis of your intercyza [marriage property settlement]. You will no doubt win, but you will more likely lose the costs, because you did not show the bailiff your documents, as Art. 38 of the Council of Ministers' regulation of 25.6.32 requires.
Mr. Leuer [probably “Leser”, reader] K. — You can demand an eviction, because handing over bills of exchange for rent without redeeming the bills does not mean that the rent has been paid; it is only a prolongation.
Mr. M. L. — Under the present procedure one cannot appeal in lawsuits up to 100 złoty, unless certain legal errors have been made.
Mr. “Official” — As you write, your working hours were not exactly fixed; you therefore have weak chances of winning the lawsuit over overtime, since you yourself disposed of your time.
Mr. “Merchant G.” — Under the present practice of the courts the date on which the cheque was issued is of no importance; it is enough that it had no cover on the payment date.
Mr. “Landlord” — If the tenant demanded that you cover the old rent with the money he sent, you cannot credit it against the current rent.
R. R.

„Cry out for help, so that the whole world will hear!“

An escaped Jew tells of the terrible tortures of Jews in Germany.
These days a Jew from Germany came here, with whom the writer of these lines had a conversation about the situation of the Jews in Germany. For understandable reasons we do not give his name or the place where he lived.
— What the newspapers write about Germany — our informant begins — cannot yet be compared to what is happening in reality. I will tell you only — he says — one of the hundreds of facts, and you will already have an idea of what the Jewish situation looks like.
In a certain town a group of Hitlerites entered[?] the home of a menaker [a porger, who removes forbidden veins and fat from meat] at the moment when he was wrapped in tallit and tefillin and praying. For this „sin“ he was arrested, and in a closed carriage (where on the way he was beaten murderously) he was taken off to the so-called „Green House“.
In the „Green House“ he was forced to stand bent double, and the wild beasts in human form beat him with rubber truncheons braided with wire.
When the menaker collapsed to the ground from the great pain, as punishment they stripped him naked, laid him face down on a long table, and after binding his head with the tallit they began — to beat him with large rubber truncheons on his naked body.
When the menaker lost consciousness, the beasts poured water over him and revived him in order to continue further bestial deeds.
Then the beasts poured salt into the deep raw wounds on his naked body and afterwards pressed the salt into the open wounds with pieces of wood.
After the inquisitorial tortures the Jew, who was writhing in agony, was thrown like a dog into another room, where he lay ill for several months.
German Jews — says the informant — are afraid to utter a word, but the Jewish press must tell the truth and „cry out for help, so that the whole world will hear“.

Telegram from the Sosnowiec kehilla to the League of Nations about the Hitlerite murders / Today: the oath of the Jewish soldiers / Bishop Kubina calls for living in peace with the Jews / The Englard–Markowicz trial before the Sosnowiec district court / On Sunday the „Keren Hayesod“ campaign begins in Sosnowiec

This week the kehilla administration in Sosnowiec sent a telegram to the League of Nations about the murders committed against the Jews in Germany.
—o—
Today: the oath of the Jewish soldiers.
Today, Friday, at 11 a.m., the oath of the Jewish soldiers will take place on the grounds of the Będzin military barracks.
The oath will be administered by the Rabbi of Będzin. In honour of the occasion a divine service will be held in the synagogue at 9 o'clock.
—o—
Bishop Kubina calls for living in peace with the Jews.
This week Bishop Kubina [Teodor Kubina, Bishop of Częstochowa] stayed in Zagłębie. As we are informed, in his sermons he called for living in peace with the Jews.
—o—
The Englard–Markowicz trial before the Sosnowiec district court.
On Wednesday the 24th of this month the trial against Alter Markowicz will be heard for the third time before the Sosnowiec district court; he was charged by Rabbi Englard with issuing, during the kehilla elections, a leaflet in which Rabbi Englard was insulted.
—o—
On Sunday the „Keren Hayesod“ campaign begins in Sosnowiec.
Next Sunday the campaign for the „Keren Hayesod“ begins in Sosnowiec. In connection with this, several meetings of prominent Zionist activists were held during this week in the premises of the „Merchants' Association“ („Sokhrim Fareyn“), which worked out the plan of the forthcoming „Keren Hayesod“ campaign.
Delegated to the campaign is the distinguished guest Adv. A. Lewinson, who holds a leading position as one of the ideologues of the Zionist labour movement „Hitachdut“. Known as a brilliant publicist in the Zionist world press and as a profound theoretician, he became known through his many pamphlets and above all through his important work „Di begrindung fun tsionizm“ („The Foundation of Zionism“); his intensive national and public work also showed itself in his having been for a long time a Sejm[?] deputy and later vice-president of the municipality in the town of Brisk [Brześć].
The direction of this year's campaign has also been entrusted to the well-known Zionist activist Mr. Jakub Gorzałka[?], who with his Keren Hayesod campaigns in Będzin succeeded in winning the sympathy of all circles of society; all this promises that this year's Keren Hayesod campaign in Sosnowiec will be carried out with great success.
In honour of the distinguished guests, the women's organisation „WIZO“ is preparing a tea reception on Saturday night in the premises of the „Merchants' Association“.

Notes of the Week

[World — news of the week; Germany and the Jews.]
The American League for the Defence of Jewish Rights has proclaimed a boycott of German goods and ships.
—o—
The world press is sounding the alarm that the danger of war is hanging in the air.
—o—
At the University of Czernowitz anti-Jewish riots have broken out. Jewish students were badly beaten.
—o—
Hitler's envoy, Rosenberg, left London in great disgrace. The train in which he travelled was pelted with rotten eggs.
—o—
President Roosevelt has sent to 55 states of the whole world an appeal in which all states are called upon to conclude a lasting peace.
—o—
The Bavarian minister Dr. Frank was expelled from Austria, where he had come on a visit.
—o—
Mass petitions have arrived at the League of Nations from all over the world against the rightless situation of the Jews in Germany.
L.O.P.P. Celebrations in Zagłębie

[Będzin and Sosnowiec — air defence; kehilla.]
On Sunday the celebrations in honour of the 10th anniversary of the L.O.P.P. [Air and Anti-Gas Defence League] began. The celebrations opened with divine services and parades.
In Będzin a number of organisations and the school youth took part in the parade, with their orchestras at the head.
Great interest was aroused in Będzin on Sunday by the attraction of a gas attack on the town.
Already at 2 o'clock in the afternoon the L.O.P.P. detachments with their gas masks began to gather on the "Sokół square".
At the same time the gases were released. The buildings of the Starostwo and the Sejmik were covered with clouds of smoke and heavy shooting was heard. It was said that the enemy's aeroplanes were being fired upon.
At the signal of the "siren" the firemen also arrived at the Starostwo building and began spraying water.
First aid of the "Red Cross" stood ready.
In connection with the jubilee, on Tuesday evening, a consultation of the kehilla representatives took place in the premises of the Sosnowiec kehilla, with the participation of the chairman of the L.O.P.P. committee in Sosnowiec, Karamanik [?], and Mr. [?] Elster, who lectured on the great importance of supporting the campaign for the benefit of the L.O.P.P.
After the lecture it was resolved to start a broad campaign among the Jewish population of Sosnowiec. For this purpose the town will be divided into districts, in order to carry out the campaign properly.
A Letter from Bystra

[Bystra — summer resort; letter.]
Bystra, which is known as the most beautiful area in the Beskids, is, thanks to its mild mountain air, recommended as a health resort for everyone, especially for convalescents who have gone through serious and light illnesses.
The local council in Bystra has lately been endeavouring to install various amenities for the guests staying here during the summer-holiday season. Besides the library that has existed until now, a library has also been opened which is supplied with the newest literature, for a minimal fee.
On the promenades the number of benches has been increased, so that the guests can rest.
There is also a cinema, a confectionery where dances are held, and Jewish guesthouses, among which the guesthouse of Mrs. Frenkel has made a name for itself among the Jewish intelligentsia.
The local population is very quiet. At the times when in some places disturbances took place on the part of the local inhabitants, Bystra was an exception in this respect, because the local population does not concern itself with "political" matters.
A considerable improvement as regards travel has also come about with the new timetable.
Ger ve-Toshav ["Stranger and Resident" — pen name].
Windows Smashed in the Częstochowa Synagogue

[Częstochowa — antisemitism.]
In the night from Saturday to Sunday young hooligans tried to break into the Częstochowa synagogue. When the attendants put up resistance, the hooligans began throwing stones and smashed several window panes of the synagogue.
"We Jews Swear!"

[Czechoslovakia — boycott of German goods.]
How Czech Jews are conducting the boycott against German goods.
We give an appeal to the Jews of Prague, which reads as follows: "We Jews swear"! Until full redress of the wrong that has been done to the German Jews and of the insult that has been inflicted on the whole of Jewry:
1) To travel to Germany only in case of the greatest necessity.
2) Not to buy any goods in Germany.
3) Not to use at all any German products.
4) Not to travel on any German ships and not to ship goods on them.
5) Not to insure ourselves even with the safest German insurance companies.
6) To copy this out and pass it on to acquaintances.
Jews, prove that you have character!
Attack by Recruits on Jews in Szczekociny

[Szczekociny — antisemitism; a pogrom averted.]
The Jewish population of Szczekociny experienced a pogrom atmosphere last Friday. It happened for the following reasons:
On Friday at 1 o'clock in the afternoon, after the closing of the draft [pobór] commission, the recruits from the village of Ye-Shandu [?] got drunk and went on a rampage in the market, accosted Jewish passers-by and began to beat them; the local Jewish population began to close its shops out of fear of a pogrom and of the looting of the shops. A group of young Jewish men put up strong resistance; police soon arrived on the spot and arrested the hooligans. Thus, thanks to the przodownik [police sergeant] [?] together with the policeman Mr. Karch [?], the pogrom atmosphere was liquidated.
Afterwards a commission headed by the starosta came here in order to investigate the matter.
Zecharit [?] Esprajcher.
Dr. Chaim Arlosoroff in Zagłębie

[Zagłębie — Zionism; lecture.]
Dr. Chaim Arlosoroff, chairman of the Executive of the Jewish Agency in Jerusalem, who is now staying in Europe on important matters, will on his way Berlin — Warsaw stop in Zagłębie on Thursday the 25th of this month, where he will appear with a lecture.
The lecture of such a Jewish personality will undoubtedly arouse due interest.
A branch of a charitable society founded in Dąbrowa

[Dąbrowa — charity.]
Thanks to the initiative of Mrs. Ingsz. Kaha [?], with the participation of the ladies Puterka, Lejtner, Mittelman, Maneta [?], Sztajnberg, Oppenheim, Rechnik and Silberschatz [?], a branch of the society "Dobroczynność" ("Charity") has opened in Dąbrowa [Górnicza].
The task of the branch is to recruit members — who already number 130 — and to place orphans in the Będzin "Orphans' Home".
Polish merchants in Zawiercie proclaim the slogan "Swój do swego"

[Zawiercie — anti-Jewish boycott.]
A meeting of Polish merchants took place in Zawiercie. At the meeting a delegate of "Rozwój" delivered a lecture in which he called on those assembled to keep, at the present moment, to the slogan: "Swój do swego po swoje" ("Each to his own — buy from your own").

[Żarki — Zionist sport and culture.]
This Saturday at 9 in the evening a large concert will take place in the fire brigade hall in Żarki, performed by the music section of the Będzin "Hakoah" under the direction of Mr. Barenblat.

[Upper Silesia — chronicle.]
Protest meeting against the book-burnings in Germany.
On Sunday a large protest meeting against the [book] bonfires in Germany took place in the Katowice synagogue.
Rabbi Dr. Chameides gave a long speech rich in content, in which he said among other things "that it is simply a disgrace for a cultured person to use the language of that barbaric nation.

The help of the Katowice Jews for the Jewish refugees from Germany.
The Katowice Jewish community convened a conference of all 16 Jewish communities, which are united in the general relief committee to help the Jewish refugees from Germany.
According to the report given by the vice-president of the Jewish community in Katowice, Dr. Abrahamer, there are about 200 fugitives in Upper Silesia, most of them people who had lived in Germany for 20–30 years. Before they managed to escape from the Hitlerite hell they had to endure cruel torments: they were beaten, tortured, and [suffered] various other sufferings and pains.
At the conference it was resolved to take practical steps to help the unfortunate refugees. Relief actions are being organised in all the communities and are meeting with due success.
The "B'nai B'rith Lodge" in Katowice has placed its premises at the committee's disposal, and a reading room for the refugees has been set up there. Jewish doctors and lawyers have declared that they will give them free medical and legal help.

A disaster in a coal mine in Siemianowice.
In a coal mine in Siemianowice lumps of coal and earth broke loose and buried three workers.
After a rescue action that lasted several hours, they only managed to bring one of them out, without any sign of life.
Heart-rending scenes are taking place at the site of the accident among the close relatives of the victims.

New dismissals.
This week the management of "Królewska Huta" announced that new reductions of workers will be made.
The voivode intervened so that the reduction plan be withdrawn.

Official of the starosty shoots his wife.
Cybel, 36, a clerk (referent) at the starosty in Bielsko, shot his wife dead.
Cybel came home at 5 in the morning from a binge; when his wife reproached him for it, he snatched out his Browning and shot her dead.
The murderer has been arrested.

International swindler arrested in Katowice.
In Katowice the police arrested one Szulim Himmelsztaub of Warsaw, who had been wanted by the police for a long time. The arrested man is an international swindler.

A child run over and killed.
Eight-year-old Getrura [?] Palka, while running across from one street to another in Katowice, was run over by a cart. The girl was killed on the spot.

28 thousand zł. stolen from the mail van in Rybnik.
While several sacks of money were being carried from the train to the mail van in Rybnik, a sack containing 28,570 zł. disappeared. In this connection several officials have been arrested on whom suspicion of the theft rests.

Coal-mine workers demand nationalisation of the coal mines.
A congress of the delegates of the mine workers of Zagłębie and of the Rybnik district took place in Katowice.
The congress discussed the question of the mass dismissals caused by the closing of a number of coal mines.
After the lectures by Stańczyk, Kaczmarski and others, a number of resolutions were adopted, among them that the state should nationalise the coal mines and place the entire coal production under public control with the participation of the coal-mine workers.
The congress calls on all German workers in Upper Silesia to break with the unions that have been seized by the Hitlerites and to join the union of the Polish workers.

7 months' prison for trying to bribe the border guard.
The merchant Judel Krakowski of Sosnowiec stood before the Katowice district court, charged with engaging in smuggling and with trying to bribe the border guard.
Krakowski was sentenced to 7 months in prison.

The "Success" of the Gemilut Chesed Fund.

[Będzin — institutions and community; editorial.]
(What is good with others is bad with us. — May one allow it to come to catastrophe?)
With us it is always different from all other peoples. We have to conduct ourselves in a different way from other people. What can one do, what can one make of it — it is already such a lost cause, and every word, every effort is a waste.
Against what are we saying this? Against what has come to be talked about [?] — precisely against the general meeting of the "Gemilut Chesed" [interest-free loan] fund, which has just [?] taken place in Będzin. Among other people it is an accepted rule that where there is interest there is life, and life awakens and develops and progresses; thus, in this way, the institution grows and "must" [?] the fruits it brings in the public sphere. But when there is [n]o interest, when the general meetings are held with a [mini]mum of people, it is a sign that there is [n]o interest, and then one sees no life; thus [—] in this case the institution does not stand at the proper height and consequently does not bring the desired benefit to the community, to the society it is meant to serve.
Yes, that is how it is with other people, that is how it should be, and that is understandable. But with us it is quite different: with us it must be different from all other peoples; with us one cannot measure anything at all by common sense — on the contrary, it always turns out different from what logic dictates to us. With us, when a general meeting of whatever public institution takes place, one should actually pray that it be held behind closed doors, among a minyan of people, and that it arouse no interest whatsoever in anyone. As soon as it is otherwise — as soon as people begin to take an interest in the institution, as soon as they come to a general meeting, which is a sign that there is life, that there is interest in our life — our interest is, unfortunately, never used for the good of the community, for the best of society, but only to destroy, to bury, to suppress what exists, what is beginning to live and develop. Yes, that is how it is with us, unfortunately. We see it every time, and on every occasion we have to record it.
It is therefore nonsense when people complain here that this or that general meeting aroused no interest among the broad strata of the population, and that the meeting had to take place with barely a minyan of people. From now on we must adopt a rule: that it is good so, that the fewer people come, the less interest it arouses, the better; and from today on let us not complain that it is not good when the community takes no interest, when society stands aloof. This coldness, this frozenness, this indifference is a sign that it is good so, that it could not be better, and that we cannot demand more of society.
The last general meeting of the "Gemilut Chesed" fund aroused enormous interest. Everyone came, young and old, and there was an uproar on the table and on the benches. A blind mass came, and 90 per cent did not know what to demand or what was going on at all. The whole business consisted only in Shmerl saying the opposite of what Berl wants. One could hear people talking without rhyme or reason, without knowing what they actually wanted; one saw that these were creatures who had been wound up, and that they need do no more than act differently from what the other wants, and speak differently. Nothing did they want to understand with reason, and they did not want to make the effort to understand. That is the worst of it. We understand when people come because the institution is dear to them, because it is an ideal of theirs. We understand when people come to help develop the institution, when they come to rescue it, when one sees that it faces a catastrophe. But it is quite different when people come to fight, when they come to wage war, when they set out to turn a philanthropic financial institution into a party grocery-shop, and everyone wants to have that little shop in his own pocket. That is when, here, people come to a general meeting — that is when interest is aroused. Working for the sake of politics — by all means, all the more so; working for the sake of an ideal, for its own sake — that, no. That is a matter for idlers, for loafers. So when it comes to burying an institution, people get up on their feet, and it becomes a kind of holy work for which one must sacrifice oneself and bring offerings. Let the institution go to ruin — that doesn't matter either, as long as obstinacy carries the day, as long as Shmerl defeats Berl. And we know, after all, that just as people here are indifferent and apathetic towards practical work, just so are they productive and energetic when it comes to pursuing a policy of destruction. At such a moment you will find out everything; all secrets will then be revealed, everyone will then tell about various "good deeds". That is how far [printed: "how high"] lies and hypocrisy have gone. It would have been quite different had the truth taken the place of honour.
Why then — the question arises — should one learn of illegal acts only when people quarrel? Why should one not learn of such matters before they are carried out? After all, a Gemilut Chesed fund is not a private enterprise, and as a public institution nothing may be concealed in it that causes or can cause harm. In a public institution — let alone one that deals with financial matters — one may not let a single [—] [?] fall, and if something undesirable does arise, one may not make a secret of it; it must be uncovered at once, so as to uproot it before the situation becomes contagious, chronic.
Were not the Jewish banking institutions destroyed in just this way? People wanted to cover up everything, to veil everything, so that public opinion, God forbid, should learn nothing — and meanwhile. Meanwhile the air was poisoned behind closed doors, and there people not only did not want to save, not only did not want to improve, but on the contrary: knowing that the mass knew nothing, they committed fresh embezzlements and illegal acts; what should never have been allowed, they allowed — and so they broke the neck, and we lost one bank after another.
The banking institutions were buried in such a scandalous way that today no merchant has a public bank where he could get a bill of exchange discounted; now the middle class has become so impoverished that it must turn to a Gemilut Chesed fund, the only such institution in town. And the question arises: can we afford such a luxury? Can one now pursue a policy of destruction in order to remove this necessary institution from the Jewish street? Do responsible people realise what a catastrophe that would be for the town? And that they have set out on this path — one can see with one's own eyes.
Possibly many will say that the devil is not as frightening as we paint him, that things are not at all so catastrophic and the fear is groundless. To this, however, one must answer that we must already now look with open eyes, and looking thus, not wanting to fool ourselves, one foresees the catastrophe at its very beginning; for one can save only while it is still early, while it is not yet dangerous; but later, once it has entered the great "gedulos" [?], there is nothing left to save: then the whole body is already sick, and with the best will, with the greatest efforts, the catastrophe must come.
An institution is exactly like a building, like a house, which must be looked after and kept in order; if one does not do so, it becomes neglected. Of course the passer-by, the casual visitor, the stranger will not [see] the neglect; but it is worse when the innermost insider too does not want to see it and imagines that it will always look the same. That is the element that fools itself and thinks it is fooling the other. Meanwhile one brick after another begins to fall, and then people set about repairs — but by then it is too late: everything is already rotten through and full of holes, and there is nothing left to save.
If one wants to repair defects, it must be done at the very beginning, and one must not wait until the bricks start falling on one's head and one hole becomes bigger than the next; for such repairs one would then need too much strength, and as usual by then people are exhausted and have no possibility of restoring the building or the institution to the level at which it formerly stood.
Exactly the same happened with our financial institutions: when they could have been saved, a policy of extermination was pursued, and later, when everything was already rotten, people set about saving them — but then it was already too late and nothing could succeed. Had people become intensive and devoted at the very beginning, what was necessary for the rescue would no doubt have succeeded.
The same now holds for the Gemilut Chesed fund: it is a rescue institution, and its situation now is such that it must be rescued, and this must be done while there is still time, while the body is not yet rotten through.
Let people take account of all this, let them reckon the consequences that quarrels and back-alley politics can bring, let them take all this into consideration, let them be sincere and not allow this necessary institution to be brought to ruin — which would be a misfortune for the town — and those who led it astray would have to be branded as criminals.
R. Let.
Between Ourselves.

(Letter to a friend).

Third letter.

My dear friend!
The Endeks [Polish National Democrats] argue: how can the Jews be good Polish citizens if they do not want to break the habit of speaking Yiddish, which is after all nothing but a German jargon?

I am ready[?] to bet the richest Endek, ten to one, that even if we were all to speak like Słonimskis and Tuwims [Antoni Słonimski and Julian Tuwim, Polish poets of Jewish origin] and talk in the language of the "Wiadom. Literackie" [Wiadomości Literackie, the Warsaw literary weekly], it is precisely then that they would raise a cry to heaven that we are Judaizing the Polish language.

And why bet, when I have a living witness: Hitler's charge in Germany against our Heines and Börnes [Heinrich Heine and Ludwig Börne]!

And as for the Germanness of Yiddish — that is a genuine gentile's error.

Just now, walking in the street, I caught a Yiddish phrase: "ikh vel aykh zogn" [I'll tell you], and in German it would be: "ich werde Ihnen sagen"; but in the [—] case it came out as "glaykh [—]", and in German it comes out "bish[—]" — a fine[?] resemblance!

Certainly "table" and "house" and "chair" and "eat" and "drink" and "sleep" and similar homely everyday notions resemble each other in both languages; but if so, then Polish also resembles Russian, since both stem from one Slavic source, and "table" and "chair" and "eat" and "drink" and "sleep" and "man" and "God" and "angel" and "devil" and "paradise" and "hell" are exactly the same — a far greater resemblance than between Jews[?] and German!

When people here were expecting the German occupation any day [1915], the half-assimilated, Russified Jews laughed at us Yiddishists. Here comes the German — they said — and your Yiddish will vanish like smoke. You will turn "dos" into "das", "foter" into "Vater", "morgn" into "moyen"[?] — and you will become real Germans.

And how did it turn out?

Everyone surely remembers that it was precisely with the German that the Yiddish movement grew a hundredfold stronger. Why? Partly because of the freedom that came — there was no Hitler then — and above all precisely because only on coming closer to the German did people become convinced that Yiddish and German are two separate languages, that the German does not understand Yiddish and the Jew does not understand German.

And how is one to understand it? That apart from a few hundred ordinary everyday words, the two languages have gone their separate ways, as far apart as the Euphrates from the Tigris, since[?] they came out of one corner in the Book of Genesis.

For perhaps 40 per cent of our roots are Hebraic and Slavic and Romance and Latin-Greek; in the conjugations and declensions they are as far apart as east from west, and the sentence structure — God save us! Which Jew can get through even one single ten-storey German period without breaking his teeth!

No, Yiddish is not German.

Three hundred years ago a Yiddish word was indeed a German word; but once upon a time the Poles and the Russians also spoke almost one language! What didn't once exist!?

There remains now another question: what do we need our own language for at all? Why irritate the ear of the town citizen with our otherness? We demand equality, after all — so why don't we make ourselves equal?

Well, the question is no question at all. Because a language is a matter of primary necessity. If a man were alone in the world, a kind of Robinson Crusoe, he could spare himself the art of speech entirely, because he would have no one to talk to. But when two people live together, instead of making themselves understood with gestures and grimaces, they make it easier with the mouth, through words. Now, since I live among Jews, since father and mother speak Yiddish, the shopkeeper woman speaks Yiddish, the shammes in the synagogue and the broker in the street and [?] the newspaper-seller and the life-insurance agent all speak Yiddish — I will hardly be a madman and suddenly start speaking Polish to them?

You will ask, then: why must we sit together in one Jewish gang? Why not spread out, one Jew among ten gentiles, and really speak the language of the surroundings?

Well, first of all one would have had to settle a couple of million Jews in the villages among the twenty million gentile peasants. Surely that would not have pleased our Endek friends. And in town, too, one would have had to place a few Jews among the policemen — I do not mean that two policemen should lead one Jew to the lock-up, but that among ten policemen one should be a Jew; among ten post officials and finance officials and komorniks [bailiffs] and notaries, and in the starostwo [county office] and in the voivodship office and in the officer corps, always one in ten should be a Jew. For myself I would pick a modest post of vice-commissioner in a sick fund, and perhaps I would be a feuilleton writer on a Polish newspaper, like some Słonimski or a Julian Sokołow [so printed].

But when I sit in the synagogue courtyard, where the paving stones speak Yiddish, how can I suddenly start speaking another language?

And to come back to the point: even if all the miracles happened and the handful of little Jews in Poland were scattered, spread out over all the corners and nooks of the country — we already have an example in the German Jews, for whom the miracle really did happen, and now they must learn Yiddish in Paris[?] on the Pletzl and Hebrew in Tel Aviv!

Meaning that no Jew in the world is insured against wandering one day into a Jewish alley, where he will have to pray minchah with a congregation and join in the "Kedushah" with a genuine Jewish tune.

And then that bit of Yiddish will come in very handy.

A. Gum.
Our Cry to the World — Let Us Root Ourselves in the Mother-Earth!

[Article — the catastrophe of German Jewry; the words of Dr. Chaim Zhitlowsky.] Dr. Chaim Zhitlowsky reacted to the misfortune of the Jews in Germany in his own profound and original way, in an article.
He repeats his old idea that one must repair the roof not only when the "house is burning"; that Jewish society must apply its entire energy in this direction — that the Jewish people should stand with both feet on the ground, "root itself in the mother-earth", so that no storm whatsoever could tear it out from there. He asks:
"Why have we not done this until now? Why are we not doing it now and do not want to think about it at all? To this there is, in my opinion, yet another sufficient excuse: because we have lived the whole time — and still live to this day — with illusions. With the illusion of a supernatural, divine redemption.
Later, when doubts began to tear apart [?] every illusion, the second one came about: the illusion of general human progress, of universal human justice, which will be poured out equally on us as on individual human beings — the illusion of Jewish "equal rights".
And when this illusion too began to totter, the third illusion sprang up: Eretz Israel, to which we will, as Herzl believed, transplant the Jewish communities of the entire world.
"Now we live, thank God, with all three illusions together. The largest part hopes: God will help! Fasts! "Repentance, prayer and charity"! Another part does not stop banging the cymbals and drums: "See how Eretz Israel is blooming! See what a radiant paradise is there, and see what a dark hell the lands of exile are"! And a third part, which knows that in that radiant paradise there is no room for all who need it — and because that part sees the heavy storm-clouds gathering over our heads everywhere, they warm up the formerly already half-frozen illusion of equal rights, let it boil up to steam-heat, and clamour once again, as in the forties of the last century: "Justice for every human being! Equal rights for Jews"!
"With that we may perhaps be able to prop up a little wagon, but what can we expect from it more than that [?] we can attain — even in Germany, and even if all four points of the American Jewish Congress were officially adopted — at most such a state as in Poland... What do you say about our Poland? Take it: the Polish government forbids by law all antisemitic organizations! Does one need a still nobler, still finer, still more conspicuous display of "justice toward Jews"? And — who will now still be so naive as to believe that this can improve our situation in Poland even by a hair? One can strangle and throttle us everywhere in good, kosher legality.
"So [?] — shall we stop having grievances against the non-Jewish world? No, nobody says that. No, not stop! Our human rights must not be touched. That claim we shall never give up; for it we shall always have to fight.
"But if we have still other grievances against the non-Jewish world, we shall be able to settle them with it only [?] then, when we can already stand on our own feet, when we are already so rooted in the mother-earth that no storm-wind can carry us away from it, that no downpour and no hail can break open [?] the roof over our heads. Only when we also become socio-economically equal to all other normal peoples will we be able, as equal peoples, to begin settling our international accounts.
"For this, however, we must first of all free ourselves from the three illusions. We must stop believing that in one of them, or in all three of them [?], could lie the answer to our [?] tragic problem.
"Only one claim, one demand can we now have toward the non-Jewish world, when we now hold under its nose the whole list of great men: the Heines and Börnes, with the Bergsons and the Einsteins, etc., etc., etc. — with this very list we can prove only one thing: that we are a people of culture blessed with very lofty cultural creative powers. We demand, we require, we beg: help us stand on our own feet; as a people, help us root ourselves in the mother-earth. Then your eyes too will be able to see clearly their greatness [?], and they will not be "too great in your eyes"!
"This is what should have been our cry to the world."
Notes of the Times. A Jewish Janitor...

A Jewish janitor... a Jewish janitor — it sounds like the song "Raisins and Almonds". Mothers will lull their children to sleep with it, grown-ups dream about it; it is an ideal, an unmistakable sign of civil and political equality. Who until now has had the privilege of becoming a Jewish janitor?

Jews have always striven to make their children into great scholars; they hired the best melamdim, the best teachers, went without enough food, without enough sleep, just to make something worthwhile of the children — and "something worthwhile" meant a doctor, a lawyer, an engineer, or, if it had to be less, at least a teacher, a bookkeeper. But a janitor? Upon my life, a joke! Had a Jew told his neighbour that he was thinking of making his child into a decent person and wanted to get him a post as janitor, people would have looked at the Jew with frightened eyes: had he perhaps gone soft in the head? A janitor, of all things!

And yet we have lived to see a time when the janitor's post beckons to many and enchants like a will-o'-the-wisp[?]. It's no small thing to be a janitor! Say, for instance, in So-and-so's house on Małachowskiego Street, with its large number of tenants — that is a sure livelihood, if not an ample one, and all without distraint officers, promissory notes, bailiffs (komorniks) and all the other "goodies" of the Jewish trading business.

Which Jew is granted that privilege straight away, and which Jewish landlord will go so far as to make the sacrifice of taking on a Moshe, a Shlomo or a Chaim as janitor? He will simply be unable, out of grief, to sit down to his midday meal when, looking out of the window, he sees that Shlomo, or Moshe, or Chaim — that same Jew who only recently dealt in textiles, or drilled pupils in a cheder, or even ground a barrel-organ with a descant — holding a broom in his hand, dressed in a blue apron just like Wojtek[?], and sweeping the street?

A Jewish janitor? It's only easy to say. It is a remarkably lofty ideal; it is the "And it shall come to pass in the end of days" of Jewish equality. When the time comes that Jewish landlords truly begin to feel heartache for their Jewish tenants who sit without a livelihood, and their hearts stop aching at the thought that So-and-so son of So-and-so, poor fellow, a man of good family, "a Jewish mensch", should stand with a broom in his hand and sweep the street — then a Jewish janitor will no longer be "music of the future". Then we will only have to wage, so to speak, the "political and national struggle" for the Jewish janitor; but among ourselves we will have settled it.

Today it is a matter of "raisins and almonds". Today only one side dreams of it — Jewish fathers without a livelihood, with a dozen little mouths pecking[?] at home.

A Jewish janitor!
A Jewish janitor...
What a beautiful illusion...

Moshe Mechuyav.
Rented a Dacha. (A Little Feuilleton).

Calmly, quietly, not at all as usual every year after Passover, my "missus" says to me these days:

— Well. Thank God, it's already after Lag ba-Omer — what's going to be this year with a little dacha?

At the words "a little dacha" I feel warm at heart: evidently, I think, she is adapting to the hard times and no longer demands grand things of me, just some dacha or other.

A difference of opinion develops between us: she says that since the rich will not travel this year to the Hitler-German spas, it will consequently be crowded even in our homely summer resorts, and one will have to[?] pay high prices because of them; therefore it is better to rent a dacha as early as possible.

I am against[?] this assumption: I have no faith in a boycott by the rich, I say; you see, the local Boycott Committee is working with all its strength to boycott all goods from the Hitlerite state, and still there are persons who pay no heed to it — like that one, for instance, who just bought a whole consignment of German goods.

— From such cases[?] — one draws no proof! — mine answers convincingly.

I don't want to give in, and I concede that in general the rich, or the formerly rich, will take their "cure" this year in other, friendly towns — there are still, thank God, other similar places for them to travel to — so there is no reason to fear inflated prices.

— All right, rent or don't rent — mine is already getting angry — but a flat we may surely rent; it is some kind of summer life, isn't it?...

So I have no choice, and alas[?]...

In the clean air of Będzin there floats, it seems, a "Teutonic"[?] spectre of gloom and melancholy, which the Hitlerite epidemic has carried over here — Jews have lost heart, the [—] are not renting anything to do something for their health, to enjoy the beauty of nature; very small is the number of those wishing to rent dachas.

The dacha owners, too, have changed their tune, forgotten the former salty prices, and ask much less.

There stands the owner with a Jew who has come to rent a dacha from him; the Jew offers a "price of the times"[?], and the Christian explains to him that even last year he took more for that same dacha.

The Jew bursts out: what are you comparing it to last year for? Back then Hitler was not yet chancellor, and today you read in the papers what a murderer he is! What terrible murders he commits against Jews!

— Yes, I've read it, word of honour, I've read it — he really is a true bandit (rozbójnik) — and the Christian, a simple-hearted man, sends three-storey curses to Hitler's address.

— But you are Jews, a clever people — the Christian goes on consoling him — you outlive your enemies; in Tsarist Russia you had many foes and you outlived them all; just so you will live to see Hitler's downfall too!

I agreed with this conclusion and gave a few złoty as a deposit on a dacha.

Mazel tov!

Yitzchak Chen.
Among Trees and Grass.

(From a Lag ba-Omer outing to Wojkowice) — by S. Libaszon [?].
Out into the field.
A Lag ba-Omer call. Out into free nature. Far from the city hubbub. On that day especially I badly wanted to run away somewhere, baraj [?] into the Mountains of Darkness, to become a primeval man and find myself cut off from the
— "civilized world"...
• • •
Lag ba-Omer of old.
The rebbe went out with us to the field behind the town. Every boy was "armed" with a bow and arrows, with which we waged the "war"; none of us was wounded; just for fun we got the rebbe's permission
— in honour of Lag ba-Omer.
Last Sunday they also showed us, the town dwellers, a "mock war" [an air-defence drill], but there is no comparison. That joke chills the blood in the veins; the yellow clouds of smoke frighten so terribly and announce that there are coming
— bloody times...
• • •
After an hour of dragging along behind "grandpa's" old nag, we finally reach the forest.
The Christian coachman, whom we never stop asking
— is it still far? — comforts us, and with his whip he points out to us the fluttering blue-and-white flag of the Będzin "Hakoach".
• • •
On entering the forest I began to search.
I looked for: the heads of the music section and of the board of "Hakoach", the members of the Keren Kayemet committee in Będzin, the Zionist and national public figures, and in the end
— I did not find a single one of them...
I also [—] looked for someone, I looked for
— the forest... For my mind could not grasp why the outing had to take place ansh [?] 12 kilometres from town: such "natural treasures" can be found even at our "Arimkes" [?] and in natural areas — found nearer than Wojkowice Kościelne...
